# List of international trips made by prime ministers of the United Kingdom

The following is a list of international prime ministerial trips made by prime ministers of the United Kingdom in chronological order since the start of Premiership of David Cameron in 2010.
Summary
As of 16 July 2025, the number of visits per country/territory where Prime Ministers have travelled since 2010 are:
* One: Akrotiri and Dhekelia, Albania, Algeria, Argentina, Azerbaijan, Bahrain, Cyprus, Gibraltar, Grenada, Iraq, Jamaica, Kazakhstan, Kenya, Kuwait, Lebanon, Mexico, Moldova, Myanmar, North Macedonia, Romania, Palestine, Qatar, Rwanda, Samoa, South Korea, Sri Lanka, the Vatican City, and Vietnam
* Two: Australia, Brazil, Bulgaria, Finland, Hungary, Iceland, Israel, Libya, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malaysia, Nigeria, Oman, Pakistan, Singapore, and Slovakia
* Three: Denmark, Indonesia, Latvia, Malta, and South Africa,
* Four: Austria, China, the Czech Republic, Egypt, Jordan, Norway, and Turkey
* Five: Canada, Estonia, Ireland, Japan, and Spain
* Six: India and Sweden
* Seven: the Netherlands
* Eight: Saudi Arabia, and Ukraine
* Nine: Afghanistan
* Ten: Switzerland
* Eleven: Poland
* Thirteen: the United States
* Thirty-two: Germany
* Thirty-seven: France
* Eighty-four: Belgium

David Cameron (2010–2016)
David Cameron made 148 trips to 62 countries (in addition to visiting the Occupied Palestinian Territories) during his premiership. In January 2013, Cameron became the first incumbent Prime Minister to visit Algeria post-independence.
Theresa May (2016–2019)
Theresa May made 77 trips to 33 countries during her premiership.
Boris Johnson (2019–2022)
Boris Johnson made 26 trips to 18 countries during his premiership.
Liz Truss (2022)
Liz Truss made two overseas trips to two countries during her premiership.
Rishi Sunak (2022–2024)
Rishi Sunak made 24 international trips to 22 countries during his premiership. In June 2023, Sunak became the first incumbent Prime Minister to visit Moldova.
Keir Starmer (2024–present)
In October 2024, Starmer became the first incumbent Prime Minister to visit Samoa. In February 2025, Starmer became the first Prime Minister since the UK left the European Union to address the European Council. In May 2025, Starmer became the first incumbent prime minister to visit Albania.
